speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; please describe exactly where the pain is located and how it started. Did this occur after a specific injury, like a fall or a twist, or did it come on gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. Based on the pain in your right thumb and wrist radiating to the elbow, worsening with infant holding, and your history of a fall six months ago, I suspect inflammation of the tendons on the thumb side of your wrist. I recommend a REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of the right wrist to rule out any fracture or arthritis from your fall, followed by a REQUEST IMAGES of the wrist tendons if symptoms persist despite treatment. Would you like to proceed with these tests, or do you have any other questions about your symptoms?
